headline: Sequence foundation models are benchmarked and pretrained for biomolecular prediction
label: Biomolecular Representation Learning
summary: Genome language models are being evaluated on resistance prediction and pretrained with evolutionary objectives, moving beyond architecture alone.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of sequence-trained deep models as representations for biomolecular prediction, with increasing attention to pretraining objectives and evaluation. BIG-TB benchmarks DNA and protein foundation models on over 17,000 M. tuberculosis genomes with resistance phenotypes, assessing both prediction and interpretability. A preprint adds evolutionary-rate prediction as a pretraining task for genome language models, composable with sequence reconstruction. A published study applies a language model to design prokaryotic cis-regulatory elements. METEOR is adjacent rather than part of this thread: it couples deep-learning enzyme confidence scores with a MILP formulation to jointly reconstruct genome-scale metabolic models. What is new is the shift from architecture alone toward biologically motivated training objectives and evaluation criteria.
